page.layout: One column of running text, full width. No marginal notes, no footnotes, no catchword or signature. Running head at top, page number at top right.

main_text.p: standi ut occasionem cito nanciscaris, Deum Opt. Max. & ego efflagito, & omnes literati deprecantur; quæ aberrata fuerunt in ἀπογράφῳ[?] Samaritano, quod mihi misisti, quoniam ita desiderasti, lubens transmitto: ista exscripta fuerunt ex cap. 12. Deuter. à v. 27. ad finem cap. facile autem hæc reperies, si sectiones libri tui sectionibus libri mei respondeant. Dividunt Samaritani singulos libros Mosis in varias sectiones, quas קצין[?] vocant, quæ parasc his[?] Judæis longe breviores sunt; librum quintum, qui nobis est Deuteronomium in 166. Katsin distinguntur, quarum 71. ab initio versus 29. atque ab his verbis incipit אני עקריהוה[?] initio igitur, ver. 27. ואדמה sanguinem [?]irrepsit, dicendum enim רם[?] ut paulo post, vel רמה[?] Nomen illud, ut scriptum est, terram significat vel rubedinem; fieri tamen potest, ut Aleph sit hæmanticum in eo nomine, ut aliquando Chaldæis, in fine vers. 28. באות[?] ponitur pro Hebræo-Samaritano בעיני[?] in oculis, suspicor scriptum esse, בהאות[?] in præ-sentia,

page.notes: Running head and page number are printed in the header; the page number reads as 198 but is doubtful, hence [?]. The Greek word ἀπογράφῳ and the Hebrew words (קצין, אני עקריהוה, רם, רמה, באות, בעיני, בהאות) are hard to read at this scan resolution and are marked [?]. The leading "N" before "irrepsit" is unclear and may be a Hebrew letter. "parascbis" is a doubtful reading of "parashis". The word "sanguinem" is italic. The right side of the scan shows the edge of the neighbouring page and show-through, which were left out.
